invariants.title: Floating Chrome Stability
invariants.risk: The floating provider opens, but expected controls or provider tabs disappear or move into an unusable state.
invariants.notes: The acceptance scenario checks floating top controls, icon-only provider tabs, active provider, and embedded header hiding.

invariants.title: Provider Selection Persistence
invariants.risk: Switching provider in floating mode does not survive storage or docking, so the sidebar opens the wrong provider.
invariants.notes: The scenario switches to Claude, asserts storage, docks, and asserts the sidebar provider.

invariants.title: Ask Auto Submit Semantics
invariants.risk: Ask captures the question but fails to send it to the provider, sends a prompt without context, or disables auto-submit for the initial handoff.
invariants.notes: The scenario checks the ask panel, floating reference question, auto-submit flag, submitted flag, and prompt length.

invariants.title: Docked Sidebar Continuation
invariants.risk: After docking, a later selection action reopens floating state or reloads the sidebar provider home page instead of continuing the existing provider session.
invariants.notes: The scenario asserts the submitted conversation URL, sends a second selection to the sidebar provider, asserts the URL is preserved, and checks floating remains hidden.

invariants.title: Private Source Redaction
invariants.risk: Localhost, loopback, or private-network URLs leak into provider prompts from development or internal pages.
invariants.notes: Unit coverage checks source URL formatting rules; acceptance coverage checks the fake provider does not receive the local fixture URL.

invariants.title: Fake Provider Boundary
invariants.risk: Fake-provider acceptance can pass while a real provider changes DOM/editor behavior and breaks injection or auto-submit.
invariants.notes: Run npm run test:acceptance:real:setup once to create a usable live-provider profile, then run the real-provider smoke command. The smoke records editor_ready, auth_required, or anti_bot_blocked so provider/session blockers are not confused with fake-provider regressions. The DevTools MCP smoke installs the unpacked extension into a dedicated real Chrome profile and classifies provider state separately from extension toolbar/floating behavior.

invariants.title: Sidebar Direct Routing
invariants.risk: A user who configured sidebar mode still gets floating UI, or sidebar opens but misses the selected prompt.
invariants.notes: The scenarios assert sidePanel open mode, sidebar provider injection, auto-submit behavior for Ask, local URL redaction, and floating hidden state.

invariants.title: Toolbar Template Integrity
invariants.risk: Explain, Translate, or Summary can silently send raw text or the wrong instruction template.
invariants.notes: Each action scenario asserts the provider received the action-specific instruction prefix and did not receive a local fixture source URL.

invariants.title: Switched Floating Provider Injection
invariants.risk: After switching provider in floating mode, the next prompt can target the old provider or reuse stale selected text.
invariants.notes: The scenario switches to Claude, selects a different paragraph, then asserts Claude receives the new selection.

invariants.title: Embedded Auth Fallback
invariants.risk: A provider sign-in wall, especially ChatGPT with Google OAuth, can trap the user inside the floating iframe with no working redirect path.
invariants.notes: The provider-boundary acceptance scenarios use fake provider auth-wall mode and assert both floating and docked auth helpers. The background normal-tab opening path is covered by tests/service-worker.test.js.

invariants.title: Dock Float Mutual Exclusion
invariants.risk: The docked side panel and the page floating window can remain visible at the same time, leaving duplicate provider sessions and confusing controls.
invariants.notes: The acceptance scenario opens a floating provider, opens the side panel through the background path, then asserts the floating surface is hidden.

invariants.title: Provider Rotation Send Coverage
invariants.risk: Provider switching can look correct visually while later Send, Explain, Translate, Summary, or Ask actions still target the previous provider or reuse the wrong prompt template.
invariants.notes: The acceptance scenario rotates through Claude, Gemini, Google, Grok, and DeepSeek and asserts provider-specific prompt receipt for Explain, Translate, Summary, Ask auto-submit, and raw Send.
